To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inulin can be used to glycate WPI with limited extent of reaction, resulting in improved heat stability of Wpi without undesirable color development.

the glycation of WPI with inulin at 6:1 ratio by freeze drying followed by dry-hearing at 80°C, 12 h without controlling relative humidities can be used to prepare conjugates with limited but desirable extent reaction and improved heat stabilities.

heat stability of whey protein isolatess can be improved by glycation with inulin under the optimized reaction conditions without undesirable changes in the rheological properties of the protein solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of reaction conditions for the glycation of whey protein with inulin.
the development of a new method for improving heat stability of WPC by conjugation with inulin.
the optimization of reaction conditions for glycation between WPI and inulins to produce a heat stable WPI-inulin conjugate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inulin is a good choice for glycation with whey protein and the glycation can improve the heat stability of whey protein without undesirable color development and significant changes in flow behaviors.
inulin can improve heat stability of whey proteins by a limited glycation reaction, and the reaction conditions can be optimized by visual observations.
glycation between whey proteins and inulin at a weight ratio of 1:6, 4:6, and 6:6 can be achieved by freeze drying and dry-heating at 80°C and 12-72 h.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inulins are effective in stabilizing whey proteins and that inulins can be used in the production of functional whey proteins.

the glycation between WPI and inulins can be optimized to achieve the limited extent of glycation without the formation of advanced Maillard reaction compounds, thus improving the heat stability of W PI.
the conjugate of WPI and dietary fiber inulin can be produced with limited glycation, which improves the heat stability of the protein and may be used as food ingredients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

inulin, an abundant dietary fiber, is an ideal candidate for glycation to improve heat stability and functionality of whey proteins without the undesirable formation of advanced Maillard reaction compounds.
glycation of WPI-inulin at 2: 1, 4 :1, or 6:1 by dry heating at 80°C and 12 to 48 hours can improve the heat stability of WPL without undesirable color development and viscosity increase.
the extent of glycation is limited by controlling reaction conditions and the extent of reaction has a great impact on the properties of glycated protein.
